summary: TaskList is only partially aligned with the TS baseline. The Go implementation matches the visible happy-path text for ordinary tasks and now filters internal tasks plus completed blockers, but it still diverges on todo-v2 exposure gating, structured output data, strict empty input validation, task-row validation and migration, TS-compatible persisted task shape, path/scope resolution, metadata/read-only/prompt behavior, task-list lifecycle notifications, ordering, teammate tool availability, and focused regression coverage.

gaps.title: TaskList is registered unconditionally instead of following the TS todo-v2 enablement gate
gaps.description: TS exposes TaskList only when todo-v2 is enabled: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS force-enables it, otherwise interactive sessions enable it and non-interactive sessions hide it. Go builds RuntimeScope with the same interactive state and even has IsTodoV2Enabled(), but SetupRegistry registers TaskCreate/TaskList/TaskUpdate/TaskGet unconditionally.
gaps.impact: Go can advertise and execute TaskList in SDK/headless/non-interactive modes where TS would not expose it, changing model planning, ToolSearch discovery, and task-vs-todo behavior.

gaps.title: Structured TaskList result data and output schema are missing
gaps.description: TS call() returns structured data shaped as {tasks:[{id,subject,status,owner?,blockedBy}]}, then mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam renders the model-facing text. Go TaskList directly renders text through StringResponse and the ToolResult/registry conversion path has no TaskList payload equivalent.
gaps.impact: Any Go caller that needs the TS output schema, parity fixtures that compare tool data, UI/state code that wants typed tasks, or post-hook/result-storage code that should distinguish data from rendered text cannot match TS behavior.

gaps.title: The TS strict empty input contract is not enforced
gaps.description: TS uses z.strictObject({}), so TaskList takes no parameters and rejects unknown properties at schema validation time. Go publishes an empty object schema but has no additionalProperties/strictness field and Execute ignores the input map entirely, so extra input keys are silently accepted.
gaps.impact: Malformed or hallucinated TaskList inputs can pass in Go while TS rejects them. That can hide prompt/schema regressions and makes tool-call validation behavior non-identical.

gaps.title: TaskList reads unvalidated task rows and does not apply TS status migrations
gaps.description: TS listTasks() routes every row through getTask(), which migrates ant-only legacy statuses and safeParse-validates the TaskSchema before including the row. Go list() unmarshals directly into TaskItem, keeps status as an unconstrained string, and TaskList renders whatever survives JSON unmarshal.
gaps.impact: Go TaskList can show corrupted, incomplete, or legacy-status rows that TS would hide or normalize, including statuses outside pending/in_progress/completed even though TS TaskList's output schema restricts status.

gaps.title: Go-created task JSON omits empty dependency arrays required by TS TaskSchema
gaps.description: TS TaskSchema requires blocks and blockedBy arrays. Go initializes those slices on create, but TaskItem tags both fields with omitempty, so a normal task with no dependencies is persisted without blocks:[] and blockedBy:[]. The existing Go persistence test checks only that the file exists.
gaps.impact: Tasks created by Go can be rejected by TS getTask/listTasks safeParse, so cross-runtime TaskList can silently drop the most common Go-created rows.

gaps.title: Task-list and task-id path sanitization does not match TS
gaps.description: TS sanitizePathComponent replaces each disallowed character with '-' and preserves the resulting string. Go replaces disallowed runes but then trims leading/trailing '-' and maps an empty sanitized value to 'default'.
gaps.impact: TaskList can read a different task-list directory than TS for IDs with punctuation, leading/trailing invalid characters, or empty sanitized values; punctuation-only IDs can collapse to default in Go.

gaps.title: Task-list scope resolution is only partially aligned for teammate and leader-team lifecycle cases
gaps.description: TS getTaskListId precedence is explicit task-list env, in-process teammate context, process/dynamic team name, leaderTeamName set by TeamCreate, then current session ID; changing leaderTeamName notifies task subscribers. Go RuntimeScope handles explicit env, TeamName(), and SessionID(), but there is no AsyncLocalStorage-equivalent teammate context, no leaderTeamName notification path, and the fallback is literal 'default' when no session resolver is wired.
gaps.impact: TaskList can resolve a different directory in in-process teammate, team-leader, resumed/early-session, or test contexts, and UI/runtime consumers may not notice that the active task list changed.

gaps.title: TaskList metadata, prompt, read-only, and result-size surfaces are incomplete
gaps.description: TS gives TaskList the exact description 'List all tasks in the task list', a long prompt, searchHint 'list all tasks', maxResultSizeChars=100000, shouldDefer=true, isConcurrencySafe=true, isReadOnly=true, and renderToolUseMessage=null. Go has a shorter description, registry-level deferred search metadata with different hint text, concurrency safe only, and no TaskList prompt/read-only/max-result metadata path on the tool itself.
gaps.impact: Model guidance, permission/read-only treatment, ToolSearch ranking, UI tool-use display, and large-result persistence thresholds can diverge from TS.

gaps.title: Task-list update signals, watcher state, and completed-list cleanup lifecycle are missing
gaps.description: TS task mutations notify in-process subscribers, TasksV2Store watches the active task directory, hides empty lists, schedules a 5s all-completed cleanup via resetTaskList, and re-watches when the task-list ID changes. The inspected Go task store exposes direct file-backed CRUD and TaskList reads but no task-list signal, watcher store, hide/reset lifecycle, or TaskList-driven UI cache.
gaps.impact: Go can have stale or non-TS lifecycle behavior around task-list display, completed-list cleanup, and immediate refresh after create/update/delete/scope changes.

gaps.title: Visible list ordering is not the same implementation contract
gaps.description: TS listTasks() preserves the order produced by readdir/Promise.all and TaskList maps that order directly. Go sorts task rows numerically when possible, then lexicographically. That is useful, but it is not the same implementation contract.
gaps.impact: Byte-for-byte TaskList output can differ for the same task directory, especially with non-numeric IDs or filesystems whose directory order differs from Go's explicit sort.

gaps.title: Agent and teammate tool-availability rules do not restore TaskList the way TS does
gaps.description: TS removes task tools from ordinary async agents but re-allows TaskList and sibling task tools for in-process teammates so they can coordinate through the shared task list. Go has a TeamMember flag on AgentTool, but agentToolRegistryOptions does not carry it into agentToolAllowedByBaseFilters, and asyncAgentAllowedTools excludes TaskList.
gaps.impact: Go teammate/async-agent sessions can receive a different TaskList availability surface than TS, breaking the shared-task-list coordination workflow.

gaps.title: TaskList parity tests cover only the Go text happy path
gaps.description: Current Go tests assert visible TaskList text for normal pending tasks and blockedBy text after TaskUpdate. They do not lock the TS structured output, feature gate, strict empty input, invalid-row filtering/status migration, dependency-array persistence, sanitizer/scope precedence, metadata/read-only behavior, lifecycle watcher semantics, ordering, or teammate availability.
gaps.impact: The existing tests can pass while most TaskList parity gaps remain unresolved or regress later.

candidate_tasks.title: Mirror TS todo-v2 exposure gates for TaskList and sibling task tools
candidate_tasks.objective: Register TaskList only under the same todo-v2 enablement rules as TS, using CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS and the interactive/non-interactive runtime state.
implementation_steps: Use RuntimeScope.IsTodoV2Enabled or an equivalent helper before registering TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, and TaskList.
Keep TaskStop and TaskOutput outside this gate unless their own parity reports require otherwise.
Add registry tests for interactive=true, interactive=false, and interactive=false with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS truthy.
acceptance_criteria: TaskList is present in an interactive registry.
TaskList is absent in a non-interactive registry when CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS is unset or falsy.
TaskList is present in a non-interactive registry when CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS is truthy.
TaskCreate, TaskGet, and TaskUpdate follow the same gate.
risks: Existing SDK/headless tests may assume task tools are always registered and will need explicit env setup.
non_goals: Do not change TaskStop or TaskOutput availability in this task.

candidate_tasks.title: Add structured TaskList output while preserving TS text rendering
candidate_tasks.objective: Expose the TS {tasks:[{id,subject,status,owner?,blockedBy}]} result shape for TaskList and derive the visible text from that structure.
implementation_steps: Introduce an additive structured-output field or typed payload mechanism in ToolResult if one does not already exist.
Make TaskList build the TS tasks payload first, including only id, subject, status, optional owner, and filtered blockedBy.
Render visible content exactly like TS mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam, including 'No tasks found' for an empty visible list.
Ensure registry/tool-result conversion preserves the structured payload for callers that need it.
Add tests that assert both structured payload and visible text.
acceptance_criteria: TaskList structured data contains tasks[] with TS field names and no Go-only fields.
Completed blocker IDs are removed from each task's structured blockedBy array.
Internal tasks are absent from both structured payload and visible text.
Visible text remains compatible with TS for empty lists, owners, and blockedBy formatting.
risks: Structured payload support is cross-cutting; keep it optional so existing tools keep their current behavior.
non_goals: Do not add description, blocks, metadata, comments, timestamps, or activeForm to TaskList's TS structured output.

candidate_tasks.title: Enforce the TS strict no-input contract for TaskList
candidate_tasks.objective: Make TaskList reject every input key the same way z.strictObject({}) does in TS.
implementation_steps: Add TaskList-local input validation that accepts nil or an empty object and rejects any key.
Represent additionalProperties:false in the published schema if the JSONSchema type is extended to support it.
Return a tool-level input error for unknown keys without reading the task store.
Add tests for empty input, nil input, and extra-key input.
acceptance_criteria: TaskList({}) succeeds.
TaskList(nil) succeeds if the Go runtime can pass nil for an empty object.
TaskList({extra:true}) returns an input error and does not list tasks.
The published schema communicates strict empty-object semantics where supported.
risks: Changing the shared parser globally could affect many tools; prefer a TaskList-local check unless a shared strict-schema migration is explicitly planned.
non_goals: Do not change TaskCreate, TaskGet, or TaskUpdate input parsing in this task.

candidate_tasks.title: Persist TS-compatible empty blocks and blockedBy arrays
candidate_tasks.objective: Ensure Go-created task JSON includes blocks:[] and blockedBy:[] so TS TaskList can parse Go-created tasks.
implementation_steps: Remove omitempty from TaskItem.Blocks and TaskItem.BlockedBy or add custom marshaling that always emits empty arrays.
Normalize nil Blocks/BlockedBy to empty slices before every task write.
Extend persistence tests to read the JSON file and assert both fields are present as arrays.
Keep TaskList visible text unchanged for tasks with empty dependency arrays.
acceptance_criteria: A newly created task JSON file contains "blocks": [] and "blockedBy": [].
Existing non-empty dependency arrays still round-trip unchanged.
TaskList text for no-dependency tasks remains '#id [status] subject' without dependency suffix.
risks: Exact JSON golden fixtures, if any, may need updates to include required empty arrays.
non_goals: Do not add Go-only fields to the TS task schema.

candidate_tasks.title: Validate and migrate task rows before TaskList lists them
candidate_tasks.objective: Make TaskStore.list mirror TS listTasks/getTask by normalizing supported legacy statuses and excluding invalid rows.
dependencies: Persist TS-compatible empty blocks and blockedBy arrays
implementation_steps: Add a read-time validation helper for TaskItem that checks required TS fields and status enum.
When USER_TYPE=ant, migrate open->pending, resolved->completed, and planning/implementing/reviewing/verifying->in_progress before validation.
Have list() skip rows that fail validation, matching TS listTasks filtering null getTask results.
Add tests for invalid status, missing required fields, ant legacy statuses, malformed JSON, and valid dependency arrays.
acceptance_criteria: TaskList omits rows that TS safeParse would reject.
TaskList renders migrated ant legacy statuses with TS target status names.
Malformed JSON remains benign and does not produce an infrastructure error.
Valid Go-created rows still appear after the dependency-array persistence fix.
risks: Strict validation may hide legacy Go-created rows that omitted required fields; sequence after the persistence-shape task.
non_goals: Do not change TaskUpdate's status input contract except where read-time migration requires tests.

candidate_tasks.title: Align task path sanitization with TS
candidate_tasks.objective: Make Go task-list and task-id path components use the same replacement-only sanitizer as TS.
implementation_steps: Change sanitizeTaskPathComponent to replace invalid characters with '-' without trimming leading/trailing '-' and without mapping the sanitized value to 'default'.
Move default fallback decisions to scope resolution callers rather than the sanitizer.
Add table tests for representative values such as 'abc', 'a/b', '!!!', '-x-', and empty string.
Add a TaskList lookup test proving Go reads the same TS-sanitized task-list directory.
acceptance_criteria: sanitizeTaskPathComponent matches TS sanitizePathComponent for representative ASCII/punctuation inputs.
TaskList no longer maps punctuation-only task-list IDs to default.
Runtime scope fallback still resolves to a usable task-list ID when no env/team/session value exists.
risks: Existing Go task files created under trimmed/defaulted names may not be found after strict parity; if migration is needed, make it explicit and backward-compatible.
non_goals: Do not change runtime background-task ID sanitization unless its own parity audit requires it.

candidate_tasks.title: Close TaskList task-list scope parity for teams and sessions
candidate_tasks.objective: Make TaskStore task-list resolution match TS precedence in explicit env, in-process teammate, process/dynamic team, leader team, and session fallback cases.
implementation_steps: Add parity tests documenting the full TS getTaskListId precedence order.
Introduce explicit teammate-context and leader-team-name hooks in RuntimeScope if TeamManager.CurrentTeamName does not cover every TS case.
Ensure standalone runtime resolves to the active session ID, not literal default, once session wiring is available.
Emit or expose a task-list changed notification if the active task-list ID changes and Go UI/runtime has a subscriber surface.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID overrides every other source.
In-process teammate context resolves to the leader/team task list.
Leader-created team name is used before standalone session ID.
Standalone runtime resolves to the active session ID.
Tests cover all precedence branches without environment bleed.
risks: Go may not have a direct AsyncLocalStorage equivalent; keep the scope API explicit and testable.
non_goals: Do not redesign TeamManager or SendMessage routing beyond task-list ID resolution.

candidate_tasks.title: Expose TaskList metadata, prompt, read-only, and result-limit parity
candidate_tasks.objective: Represent TaskList's TS model guidance and runtime metadata in Go.
implementation_steps: Change TaskList.Description() to the TS description text.
Add optional interfaces or metadata for read-only status, maxResultSizeChars, prompt text, and renderToolUseMessage suppression if the Go runtime lacks them.
Return TaskList read-only=true and maxResultSizeChars=100000 through the chosen metadata path.
Align the deferred search hint with TS or add an explicit test documenting the intended delta.
Add tests for description, ToolSearch discovery metadata, read-only metadata, and result persistence threshold.
acceptance_criteria: TaskList's model-facing description matches TS.
TaskList exposes read-only=true to the Go permission/runtime layer.
TaskList large-result persistence uses a 100000-character threshold.
TaskList tool-use display is suppressed where Go has an equivalent UI display hook.
Deferred-tool metadata remains present.
risks: Metadata interfaces are cross-cutting; keep them optional and additive.
non_goals: Do not implement unrelated permission-policy changes for mutating task tools.

candidate_tasks.title: Restore TaskList lifecycle signals and completed-list cleanup behavior
candidate_tasks.objective: Provide Go equivalents for TS task-list update notifications, active-list watching, and completed-list cleanup where the Go UI/runtime consumes task state.
dependencies: Close TaskList task-list scope parity for teams and sessions
implementation_steps: Add a task-update signal or subscriber surface to TaskStore mutations if Go has UI/runtime consumers for task lists.
Wire create/update/delete/reset to notify subscribers without making task mutations fail on subscriber errors.
Implement a watcher/cache layer for the active task-list directory if the Go TUI should mirror TS TaskListV2 behavior.
Mirror the TS hide/reset behavior for all-completed lists after the configured delay, or document why Go intentionally omits the UI feature.
Add tests with fake timers or a small injectable clock where practical.
acceptance_criteria: TaskStore create/update/delete/reset emit a best-effort update signal.
Changing the active task-list ID causes watchers to re-point to the new directory.
All-completed task lists are hidden/reset according to the TS lifecycle when the Go UI/runtime surface is active.
Subscriber failures do not fail task mutations.
risks: Go may not yet have a TaskListV2 UI surface; if not, land only the store signal plus tests and leave UI wiring for a separate TUI task.
non_goals: Do not redesign the whole TUI around task lists in this task.

candidate_tasks.title: Align TaskList ordering with the TS implementation contract
candidate_tasks.objective: Decide and lock the exact TaskList ordering contract needed for TS parity, then update Go implementation/tests accordingly.
implementation_steps: Create a fixture with mixed numeric and non-numeric task filenames and record the TS-visible order expected for parity.
If byte-for-byte TS order is required, remove or adjust Go's explicit numeric sort to match the fixture.
If product chooses numeric ID order despite TS implementation, document that as an intentional parity exception and add tests for the chosen order.
Keep structured output and visible text in the same order.
acceptance_criteria: A TaskList ordering test covers numeric IDs, non-numeric IDs, and mixed IDs.
The order of structured tasks[] matches the order of rendered text lines.
The accepted order is either TS-compatible or explicitly documented as an intentional exception.
risks: TS relies on filesystem readdir order, which may be platform-dependent; avoid overfitting to one platform without a fixture-based decision.
non_goals: Do not change task ID allocation in this task.

candidate_tasks.title: Align TaskList availability for async agents and teammates
candidate_tasks.objective: Make Go agent registry filtering remove TaskList from ordinary async agents but re-allow it for in-process/team-member coordination like TS.
dependencies: Close TaskList task-list scope parity for teams and sessions
implementation_steps: Carry TeamMember or an equivalent teammate flag into agentToolRegistryOptions.
Keep TaskList excluded from ordinary async agents unless a profile explicitly allows an equivalent safe path.
Re-allow TaskList, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, and SendMessage for team-member/in-process teammate sessions matching TS.
Add tests covering ordinary async agent filtering and teammate async filtering.
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary async agents do not receive TaskList by default.
Team-member/in-process teammate sessions do receive TaskList and sibling coordination tools.
Existing disallowedTools/profile restrictions still override allowed task-tool visibility.
Tests explicitly include TaskList, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, and TaskCreate.
risks: Agent registry filtering is security-sensitive; preserve existing disallow/profile precedence.
non_goals: Do not broaden task-tool access for ordinary background subagents.

candidate_tasks.title: Add a focused TaskList parity regression suite
candidate_tasks.objective: Expand Go tests so TaskList parity is locked across output, validation, storage, scope, metadata, lifecycle, ordering, and agent availability.
dependencies: Can be done incrementally with the implementation tasks; tests for not-yet-fixed gaps should land alongside their fixes rather than breaking main.
implementation_steps: Add tests for visible text and structured payload with empty, owner, blockedBy, completed blocker, and internal-task cases.
Add tests for gate, strict input, sanitizer, scope precedence, invalid/migrated rows, persisted empty dependency arrays, metadata, lifecycle notifications, ordering, and teammate availability.
Keep tests isolated with t.Setenv, temporary CLAUDE_HOME, and temporary project roots.
Prefer one small test per parity contract rather than a single mega-test.
acceptance_criteria: TaskList parity tests fail for each documented gap before its fix and pass after the fix.
Tests assert both visible content and underlying structured/state behavior where applicable.
No test reads or writes the user's real ~/.claude task directory.
The suite can be run narrowly during tool parity work.
risks: Tests for unresolved gaps should be staged with their implementation tasks to avoid permanently failing main.
non_goals: Do not rewrite unrelated TaskCreate/TaskGet/TaskUpdate tests except for shared fixtures.
